issues.title: Section 4.1 (and section 8 item 7) forbid the WF-03 Step 4 regression test, leaving ISS-0227 with no legal terminal status
issues.detail: Section 4.1 declines to specify any new regression test on the ground that a test asserting a struct field's absence 'would assert this design's implementation choice rather than any behaviour of the pool', and section 8 item 7 turns that into a prohibition on ELIXIR-DEV ('Do not write any new test file'), with section 4.1 additionally telling ORCH that TEST-DESIGNER should be dispatched 'only to re-run the existing suites, not to author new cases'. That is not an omission the downstream steps can route around -- it actively blocks WF-03 Step 4. RULING: OVERRULED, on three grounds, the third of which is decisive. (i) WF-03_issue_resolving.md:99-103 requires Step 4's test to be shown to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the post-fix code, as the proof that the fix fixed something. The doc's own escape hatch at :105-117 ('when the pre-fix failure is non-existence') does not apply here -- the module exists and the fields exist, so a genuine fail-then-pass is available. (ii) The 'it pins an implementation detail' objection mistakes the defect class for a behavioural one. ISS-0227's defect IS structural: REVIEWER filed it precisely because a second stored copy of derivable state can silently diverge, and ISSUE-FIXER's own diagnosis states that this class 'is reachable only by reading, or by a structural assertion on the exact key set'. A white-box key-set assertion is therefore not a gratuitous pin -- it is the only mechanical detector of the exact hazard the issue exists to remove, and it is the standing style of this suite, which already reaches into :sys.get_state/1 at :920, :1007, :1008, :1146 and elsewhere. Section 4.1's own objection that the test 'would have to be deleted the day the field is legitimately re-introduced' is the guard working as intended: re-introduction should require a deliberate edit that confronts ISS-0227's rationale, which is exactly what silent re-introduction is not. (iii) DECISIVE: upholding 4.1 leaves ISS-0227 with no truthful terminal status. ISSUE_QUEUE.md:180-247's vocabulary is open / in_progress / resolved / instrumented / no_defect. `resolved` (:187) requires 'a root cause was actually removed, and a regression test proves it'. `no_defect` (:199-208) is false here -- a defect existed and is being removed. `instrumented` (:192-197) is false here -- the root cause IS removed, and it would additionally demand a superseded_by successor carrying remaining work that does not exist. So a design that forbids the test forces the run either to write a false `resolved` or to leave a genuinely-fixed issue non-terminal. Section 4.1's proposed evidence (a) mix compile --warnings-as-errors exiting 0 and (b) the existing suites still passing is real and should be kept, but it is absence-of-regression evidence, not proof the root cause was removed: both (a) and (b) would read identically if ELIXIR-DEV made no change at all. MINIMUM REGRESSION TEST, specified precisely enough for TEST-DESIGNER to write. One test, no new file, appended to the ISS-0224 RT block in test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs, named 'RT-9 (ISS-0227): the in-flight provision op and the in_flight record carry no duplicate of a derivable value'. Reach the observation point with the helpers the file already has and NO sleep: pool = start_pool!(max_concurrent: 1); spawn_claimer(pool, :o, 1_000); state = wait_until_pool_state(pool, "O's provisioning is in flight", &provision_in_flight?/1) -- this is the exact synchronisation :917-918 already uses. Then assert THREE things. (1) The exact key set of the in-flight provision op: bind {:provision, p} = state.in_flight.op and assert Enum.sort(Map.keys(p)) == [:from, :owner_down?, :owner_ref, :sandbox_id, :schema_name]. Use sorted-key-list EQUALITY, not refute Map.has_key?(p, :owner_pid) -- equality is what makes it a drift guard in both directions, failing both if owner_pid returns and if some future change quietly adds another undeclared field. (2) The exact key set of the record: assert Enum.sort(Map.keys(state.in_flight)) == [:op, :task_pid, :task_ref]. (3) That the derivations still reach the values, so the case documents the replacement and not merely the removal: assert elem(p.from, 0) == the claiming pid returned by spawn_claimer/3, and {:provision, %{schema_name: n}} = state.in_flight.op with assert is_binary(n). FAIL-THEN-PASS: against pre-fix code (this branch's a64159d sandbox_pool.ex, both fields present) assertion (1) fails on :owner_pid and assertion (2) fails on :schema_name; against post-fix code all three pass. TEST-DESIGNER states both runs explicitly per WF-03:99-103. COVERAGE MAP, so nothing is left unproven: RT-9 assertion (1) proves R2, assertion (2) proves R4, assertion (3) proves the section 2.2/2.3 derivations remain reachable; mix compile --warnings-as-errors exiting 0 proves R5; the existing suites passing unchanged prove no behavioural drift. R1 (the @typep line) is compile-time only and is not runtime-observable by any test -- it is discharged by ELIXIR-DEV's diff and REVIEWER, and the design should say so rather than leave it silently uncovered. REQUIRED EDITS: replace section 4.1 with the above (keeping its (a)/(b) evidence as additional, not sole, evidence), delete or invert section 8 item 7, and add RT-9 to section 7's file table as a TEST-DESIGNER-owned change to test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs -- which also means section 7's 'Explicitly NOT touched: every test file' must be narrowed to exclude that one file. With those edits ISS-0227 earns `resolved` legitimately.

round_2.summary:
PASS. All three round-1 findings are fixed, correctly, and nothing moved outside them.

NOTHING-ELSE-MOVED. `git diff --stat a64159d..4f6bac5` touches exactly two files: this handoff (round 1's own record, +88) and the design doc (+178/-22 -> 581 to 696 lines). `git diff a64159d..4f6bac5 --stat -- lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex` is EMPTY -- the module under change was not touched by the rework. The design doc's diff is 13 hunks, and their headers map exactly onto the seven regions ISSUE-FIXER listed and nothing else: :56 (W4 in 0.3), :248 / :257 / :262 / :268 / :270 / :280 (section 4's opening paragraph, the Method block, and the old 4.1 replaced by a new 4.1 plus a new 4.2), :302 (5.1's line number), :472 / :475 / :489 (section 7's file table, its 'Explicitly NOT touched' line, and post-change check 3), :509 (section 8 item 7), :564 (section 12's AC rows). There is no hunk anywhere in section 2's removal table (R1-R5), the C1-C5 instructions of section 5.2-5.7, section 3, section 6, section 9, section 10 or section 11. Confirmed untouched.

D1 -- FIXED, and the RT-9 spec matches what round 1 specified, point for point. Section 4.2 carries: the observation point built from the helpers already in the file (`start_pool!(max_concurrent: 1)`, `spawn_claimer(pool, :o, 1_000)`, `wait_until_pool_state(pool, "O's provisioning is in flight", &provision_in_flight?/1)`) with an explicit no-sleep/no-new-constant statement, and it correctly identifies that as the same synchronisation :917-918 already uses. Assertion (1) is `Enum.sort(Map.keys(p)) == [:from, :owner_down?, :owner_ref, :sandbox_id, :schema_name]` on `{:provision, p} = state.in_flight.op` -- the expected key list is exactly the five survivors of R1/R2 and is correct against sandbox_pool.ex:531-540. Assertion (2) is `Enum.sort(Map.keys(state.in_flight)) == [:op, :task_pid, :task_ref]` -- exactly the three survivors of R4, correct against :568-573. Both are stated as sorted-key-list EQUALITY with the two-directional-drift-guard reasoning spelled out, and the doc goes further than round 1 asked by explicitly ruling `refute Map.has_key?` out as 'not an acceptable substitute'. Assertion (3) carries both halves (`elem(p.from, 0)` against spawn_claimer/3's returned pid, and `is_binary(n)` on the schema name reached via `state.in_flight.op`). The fail-then-pass table names the pre-fix baseline as this branch's a64159d, marks (1) FAILS on :owner_pid and (2) FAILS on :schema_name pre-fix, and correctly reasons that WF-03:105-117's 'pre-fix failure is non-existence' escape hatch does not apply. The coverage map maps R2 -> assertion (1), R4 -> assertion (2), the 2.2/2.3 derivations -> assertion (3), R5 -> warnings-as-errors exit 0, no-drift -> the existing suites. R1 IS now stated as compile-time-only: the row says a @typep is erased at compile time, that no :sys.get_state/1 read, Map.keys/1 or dialyzer run in this project's gate can distinguish a runtime key set from a declared typespec, and that R1 is discharged by ELIXIR-DEV's diff plus REVIEWER -- named, not silently uncovered, which is what round 1 required. Evidence (a) and (b) are retained as ADDITIONAL evidence with the 'both would read identically against an empty diff' limitation stated. Section 8 item 7 is INVERTED, not merely deleted: it now reads 'Do not write RT-9 yourself, and do not skip it', assigns it to TEST-DESIGNER at WF-03 Step 4, and states that `resolved` is not truthful until its fail-then-pass is on record -- with a parenthetical recording the round-1 text it replaced. Section 7's file table gains a `test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs` row owned by TEST-DESIGNER ('RT-9 appended to the existing ISS-0224 RT block, no new file, no new helper, no new constant'), and the 'Explicitly NOT touched' line is narrowed to 'every test file EXCEPT test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs', naming the two other suites as still untouched. Section 7's post-change check 3 is also correctly amended to say RT-9 is TEST-DESIGNER's, after ELIXIR-DEV's step, so ELIXIR-DEV is not left thinking it must run a test that does not exist yet. Section 12 gains a matching AC row. Fixed completely.

D2 -- FIXED AND VERIFIED. Section 5.1 precedent 2 now cites :656. `grep -n "^## 1[12]\." lib/letflow/design/iss064-orphaned-tenant-schemas-fix.md` returns :619 for '## 11. Extension (ISS-0110, 2026-08-21)' and :656 for '## 12. Extension (ISS-0217, 2026-08-21) -- sibling test_parallel.sh partitions vs. a genuine external invocation'. Both numbers in that sentence are now right.

D3 -- FIXED, AND THE CORRECTED COMMAND REPRODUCES EXACTLY. I ran the doc's stated command verbatim: `grep -rohE --include=*.ex --include=*.exs "in_flight[a-z_]*\.[a-z_]+" lib test | sort | uniq -c` -> `7 in_flight.op`, `4 in_flight.task_ref`, `1 in_flight.task_pid`, 12 matches total, ZERO .schema_name. That is exactly the count and breakdown the doc now states, in W4 and in section 4's Method block, which agree with each other. Note the doc also dropped the `-n` from the corrected command, which is the right fix -- with -n the prefix defeats `uniq -c` entirely.

D3's EXPLANATION OF THE OLD '32' -- CHECKED, AND IT HOLDS UP; NOT A RATIONALISATION. The doc claims (i) an unrestricted run returns '~50 hits, ten of them .schema_name, all prose' and (ii) the 32 was a count of -n-prefixed lines that `uniq -c` cannot aggregate because the line-number prefix makes every line unique. Both parts tested. (ii) is mechanically true and I verified it directly: `grep -rnohE ... | sort | uniq -c` today produces 56 groups over 57 output lines -- exactly one pair collides -- so the command genuinely cannot aggregate and its output count is a line count, not a match count. (i): unrestricted today gives 57 lines of which 10 are .schema_name, matching the 'ten' exactly; and reconstructing the repo state at a64159d (31 hits everywhere except this design doc, plus 20 in the doc as it stood at a64159d, via `git show a64159d:...`) gives 51, so '~50' was accurate for the state the claim describes.
